slides.headline:
Three starred kitchens, three years.
Busan finally has a fourth.
slides.subline: Le DORER, 37 Marine City 3-ro, Haeundae-gu — the only Busan restaurant promoted to One MICHELIN Star in the Seoul & Busan 2026 guide, whose chef took the Young Chef Award the same night

slides.label: starred restaurants in the whole of Busan. Le DORER is the newest — and the city's only promotion in the 2026 guide.
slides.note: The MICHELIN Guide Seoul & Busan 2026 selected 233 restaurants: 178 in Seoul, 55 in Busan. Seoul holds 42 starred restaurants; Busan holds four, all One Star — Mori, Palate, Fiotto and Le DORER. The first three have held their star since Busan joined the guide in 2024. Sources: MICHELIN Guide selection release, Stripes Korea, Haps Korea, Busan Ilbo

items.d: Le DORER was the single Busan promotion in the Seoul & Busan 2026 selection, announced at a ceremony held at SIGNIEL Busan — the guide's tenth year in Korea

items.t: The Young Chef Award went to the same kitchen
items.d: Chef Kim Chang-uk took the 2026 MICHELIN Young Chef Award. The guide's write-up credits refined sophistication within familiar tastes, and a steady respect for seasonality and regional ingredients

items.t: Korean cooking, French and Japanese technique
items.d: The guide describes a tasting menu reinterpreting traditional Korean cuisine through a contemporary lens. Korean trade press notes the room began as a Korean restaurant before moving contemporary

items.t: Busan's entire starred list is four rooms
items.d: Mori, Palate and Fiotto have each held One Star since the guide's Busan launch in 2024, with Fiotto also keeping a MICHELIN Green Star. Le DORER is the fourth name on that list

slides.title:
A frozen list,
broken from inside.
slides.body:
The MICHELIN Guide reached Busan in 2024 with three One Star restaurants: Mori, Palate, Fiotto. The next edition kept all three and added nobody. So did the one after it. For three consecutive guides, the count in Korea's second city sat at three.

The 2026 edition moved it to four, and the interesting part is where the fourth came from. Not a Seoul dining room opening a coastal outpost, not an imported name. The guide's listing and Korean coverage describe Kim Chang-uk as a young chef from Busan, cooking a Korean tasting menu built on seasonal regional ingredients, two floors up in a Marine City building, down an alley with Haeundae Beach in view.

The French name sits on top of Korean cooking: bulgogi layered from hanwoo oxtail and scallion, a white bibimbap of bellflower root and mushroom, duck sanjeok with fermented fatsia.

And the guide held its tenth-anniversary ceremony in Busan that night — the city's first new star in three years, handed out on its own ground.

items.d: The restaurant's own site gives the address as units 213 and 214 of the Hanil Ordew building; Korean listings add the lot address Udong 1435-3. Note one Korean roundup prints a different Suyeong-gu address — the official site does not support it

The official reservation page lists lunch from 12:30 and dinner 18:00–22:00 with a break between; Korean listings put the break at 14:30–17:00. A five-day week is worth confirming before you build a trip around it
The restaurant states that all reservations are made exclusively through Catch Table's online booking. Its listed phone is +82 51-747-8522 during business hours, and email info@ledorer.com

items.t: Lunch listed at 120,000 won, dinner at 210,000
items.d: Korean listing platform DiningCode shows those course prices, with supplements such as abalone at +30,000 won. These come from a third-party listing rather than the restaurant's own page, so treat them as indicative

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked in September 2026.
slides.by:
We have not eaten here. Whether a 210,000 won dinner is worth it to you is your call, not ours.
Prices, hours, menus and booking rules change without notice — confirm directly before you go.

We only feature places we've verified are real and open.
Save this for your next trip to Busan

caption:
Busan's MICHELIN star list carried the same three names for three straight years.

Le DORER, a second-floor room off a Marine City alley, made it four — and chef Kim Chang-uk took the 2026 Young Chef Award the same night.

We haven't eaten here; a 210,000 won dinner is yours to judge.

Sources in the last slide.
